title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document is the canonical People Ops handbook section that summarizes how we hire, onboard, structure roles and career ladders, and the benefits and internal tools that every Redwooder needs to know. It is intended for new hires, hiring managers, and anyone making role or compensation recommendations.

Key contacts:
- People Ops (general): people-ops@redwood.com
- Payroll & Benefits: payroll@redwood.com
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.com
- IT & Access Requests: it-ops@redwood.com

Goals & metrics we track:
- Time-to-offer (target): <= 14 days from final onsite interview
- Time-to-fill (target): 35 days median for IC roles, 45 days for managers
- Time-to-productivity (target): 30 days to 75% ramp for ICs; 60 days for managers
- Offer acceptance rate (goal): >= 70%

Section 1 — Company & Work Model:

- Redwood is a remote-first company with hubs in SF Bay Area and London. Employees can choose fully remote or hub-based work.
- Core hours: 10:00–15:00 local time for cross-team collaboration (flexible outside core).
- Work-from-home stipend: $300/year for home office supplies; $1,200 one-time for ergonomic equipment for new hires on manager approval.

Section 2 — Roles and Career Ladders (summary):

We maintain clear IC and Manager ladders across Engineering, Product, Research, Design, and GTM teams. Career ladders are published and maintained by People Ops in partnership with each org. Below is a short summary — see the linked team-specific ladder docs for rubric details.

Common role levels (applies to most orgs):
- IC1 (Associate) — Entry-level individual contributor.
- IC2 (Engineer II / Experienced IC) — Solid contributor, owns tasks and small features.
- IC3 (Senior) — Leads features, mentors peers, shapes design.
- IC4 (Staff / Principal IC) — Cross-team technical leadership, designs systems, measurable impact.
- IC5 (Senior Staff / Principal+) — Strategic technical direction for multiple teams.
- IC6 (Distinguished / Fellow) — Company-level technical influence.

Manager ladder:
- Mgr1 (Manager) — Manages a team (4–8 people), performance, hiring, and delivery.
- Mgr2 (Senior Manager) — Manages managers or larger team, longer horizon planning.
- Dir/VP — Org leadership, strategy and cross-functional alignment.

Promotion & leveling process (high level):
1) Candidate documents impact in a promotion packet (1–2 pages).
2) Manager prepares packet with examples against rubric and proposes new level.
3) Packet is reviewed by peer-level reviewers and People Ops for calibration.
4) Promotion decision communicated; effective date is aligned with pay cycle when possible.

Criteria highlights (examples used in rubrics):
- Scope: breadth of ownership across services and teams.
- Technical or functional impact: revenue, performance, reliability improvements.
- Mentorship & leadership: direct reports, cross-team influence, mentorship.
- Execution: shipping complex systems reliably.

Section 3 — Benefits & Perks (summary):

Standard employee benefits (full-time US example):
- Health insurance: employer-subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision (carrier partners: Blue Cross, Delta Dental, VSP).
- 401(k): employer match up to 4% after 90 days.
- Equity: RSU grants on hire + annual refresh cycle.
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO (prorated first year), company-wide holiday calendar (12 days), 10 paid sick days.
- Parental leave: Primary caregiver 20 weeks fully paid; secondary caregiver 8 weeks fully paid.
- Flexible spending accounts: FSA and HSA options available.
- Wellness stipend: $200/quarter for fitness or mental health subscriptions.
- Commuter benefits: pre-tax transit/parking where applicable.
- Employee assistance program (EAP): confidential counseling available 24/7.

Perks and allowances:
- Conference & learning budget: $2,000/year per employee; team training budgets available by request.
- Snack & socials budget for hub teams.
- Referral bonus program: $5,000 for engineering hires, $3,000 for other roles (subject to change, see Recruiting incentives page).

Benefits administration & contacts:
- Enrollment window: 30 days from start date for new hires; annual open enrollment in November.
- For detailed plan docs, claims, and provider contacts see the Benefits Center (HRIS link in Related Links).

Section 4 — Hiring overview & stages:

High-level hiring process (typical for engineering roles):
1) Requisition opened in Greenhouse by hiring manager (manager must attach role description and target level).
2) Recruiter sources and screens candidates. Initial phone screen with recruiter + technical/role screen.
3) Onsite loop (virtual or in-person) — typically 4 interviews: System Design, Coding/Problem Solving, Product Sense/Domain, and Culture / Collaboration.
4) Hiring manager debrief and calibration with interviewers.
5) Hiring committee review if required (levels IC4+ and manager roles).
6) Offer and compensation approval by People Ops and Finance.
7) Background check and reference checks run after candidate accepts offer.

Standard timeline expectations:
- Recruiter screen to onsite: target 14 days.
- Offer approval process: target 3 business days once packet is complete.
- Background check: typically completes within 3–5 business days.

Interview guidance for hiring teams (quick checklist):
- Use standardized rubrics stored in the Hiring Kit.
- Interviewers must submit written feedback within 48 hours.
- Avoid last-minute canceled interviews — inform Recruiting as soon as possible.

Section 5 — New hire onboarding (first 90 days):

Pre-boarding (before Day 1):
- Recruiter/People Ops sends welcome packet with start date, first-week agenda, and benefits enrollment instructions.
- IT provisions equipment and creates Okta and Google accounts. For private deployment roles requiring dedicated hardware, provisioning is coordinated with Eng Infra and may take additional time.
- New hire receives a calendar invite for Orientation (Day 1, 09:30 PST).

Day 1 agenda (example):
- 09:30–10:30: People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, policies).
- 10:45–11:30: IT & security briefing (SSO/Okta, MFA setup, device encryption).
- 11:45–12:30: Manager welcome and team lunch (virtual or in-person).
- Afternoon: Product orientation, required trainings (security awareness, code of conduct).

30-day check-in:
- Manager performs formal 1:1 check-in and completes 30-day onboarding form. Goal: confirm access, first ticket/PR, mentoring plan.

60-day check-in:
- Focus on progress against first-quarter goals and cross-team introductions.

90-day review:
- Manager and People Ops review ramp progress; confirm role expectations and performance goals.

Day 1 checklist (short):
- [ ] Okta account created and MFA enabled.
- [ ] Email & Google Drive access validated.
- [ ] Slack access and key channels joined (#all, #eng, #people-ops, team channel).
- [ ] GitHub access to core repositories.
- [ ] Redwood Console demo and dev cluster access request submitted.
- [ ] Benefits enrollment started.

Section 6 — Internal tools & access (what to expect and how to request):

Primary tools and owners:
- Identity & SSO: Okta (IT & Security owner).
- HRIS & payroll: Workday (People Ops owner) — benefits enrollment and personal data.
- Applicant Tracking System: Greenhouse (Recruiting owner) — requisitions and candidate tracking.
- Source control: GitHub (Eng Infrastructure owner) — team repos and access controls.
- Communication: Slack (Eng Platform owner) — channels and shared boards.
- Documentation: Confluence (All hands; People Ops owner maintains this handbook).
- Observability/Operations: Datadog and Sentry (Eng Platform / SRE owners).
- Expense & travel: Concur (Finance owner).

Access request flow (IT ticket):
1) New hire access is created automatically for standard roles via onboarding playbook.
2) For special access (production keys, private clusters, on-prem hardware), manager opens a Jira Service Desk ticket and lists justification and duration.
3) Access requests for RBAC-sensitive services require approval by service owner and Eng SRE.
4) Temporary elevated access is granted for a maximum of 14 days unless extended with documented justification.

Security and compliance notes:
- All employees must complete Security Awareness training within the first week.
- MFA is enforced for all accounts.
- Production secrets must be accessed through the Secrets Manager (internal) and all access is audited.

Section 7 — Manager responsibilities for hiring and onboarding:

Hiring:
- Write clear job descriptions, define level and success metrics.
- Participate in timely interviews and give written feedback.
- Partner with Recruiting to close loops and remove blockers.

Onboarding & ramping:
- Prepare a 30/60/90 day plan and share it with the new hire on Day 1.
- Assign a buddy (peer mentor) for the first 60 days.
- Run weekly 1:1s during first 90 days and complete People Ops check-in forms at 30/60/90 days.

Performance & development:
- Provide regular feedback and sponsor development plans.
- Maintain active promotion calibration packets for candidates.

Section 8 — Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Who approves relocation offers?
A: People Ops + Hiring Manager + Finance for any relocation > $5k.

Q: Can I change my benefits outside of open enrollment?
A: Qualifying life events (marriage, birth, domestic partnership) allow outside enrollment within 30 days of the event.

Q: How do I request additional headcount?
A: Submit a requisition in Greenhouse and attach justification, draft job description, and expected budget. Manager should sync with Finance and People Ops prior to opening roles for Manager+ hires.

Section 9 — Links and documents referenced:
- Hiring Kit & Interview Rubrics: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/hiring-kit
- Benefits & Enrollment Guide: /confluence/company-handbook/benefits-center
- Promotion & Leveling Rubrics (team-specific links in each org folder)
- IT Access Playbook: /confluence/eng-infra/it-access-playbook

Appendix A — Example 30/60/90 Day Plan (template):
- 30 days: Complete onboarding trainings, ship first small PR, meet key stakeholders.
- 60 days: Take ownership of a small feature, lead a retrospective, mentor a peer.
- 90 days: Lead feature end-to-end, present impact at team demo, set goals for next quarter.

Ownership & maintenance:
- Document owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: Annually in January; immediate updates when policies or carriers change.
